name: Carlos Diegues
bio: Carlos José Fontes Diegues OMC, known as Cacá Diegues (Maceió, May 19, 1940 – Rio de Janeiro, February 14, 2025), was a Brazilian filmmaker. He was one of the founders of Cinema Novo.

credits.title: God Is Still Brazilian
credits.overview: God needs to return to Earth when celestial beings rebel against humanity and decide to launch another meteor to exterminate life on the planet.

credits.title: Cadu Barcellos: Legends never die, they live forever
credits.overview: This documentary celebrates Cadu Barcellos, a Black filmmaker from the Maré favela complex. In defiance of erasure, the film moves beyond tragedy to celebrate his light, ancestry, and legacy.

credits.title: Fernando Coni Campos: Cada um Vive como Sonha
Armando Costa: “Televisão pra Mim Não é Bico”
credits.overview: Armando Costa was one of Brazil's most successful authors, both in terms of audience and critical acclaim, responsible for shows like "A Grande Família" and "Malu Mulher." Despite this, he didn't care about fame or signing his works.

credits.title: Turn It Up, It's Rock 'n' Roll
credits.overview: The film tells the story of Luiz Antônio, a clumsy radio host, who unexpectedly finds himself in charge of a bankrupt radio station. credits.overview: Filmmaker Roberto Farias' passion for cinema is revealed by his daughter Marise Farias through an intimate look, from childhood to his political, economic and cultural role in Brazilian Cinema. credits.title: Quando a Coisa Vira Outra
credits.overview: Vladimir Carvalho's Cinema of Inequality marked the documentary filmmaker's trajectory over decades of activity. Considered one of the most important Brazilian documentary filmmakers in activity, his images influenced the emergence of Cinema Novo and the new Brazilian documentary years later. credits.title: Dr. Gama
credits.overview: Based on the biography of Luiz Gama, one of the most important characters in Brazilian history, a black man who used the laws and courts to free more than 500 slaves. credits.title: The Good Cinema
credits.overview: An authentically marginal cinema created in Catholic university in Brazil. One of the most intriguing and imaginative moments in modern cinema in the voice of some of its select conspirators—with Carlos Reichenbach at the lead—, and through the most razing flow of images that can possibly be conceived.

credits.title: Torquato, Imagem da Incompletude
credits.overview: A reflection on the works and thinking of the last years of production by Torquato. Such as the magazine "Navilouca", the film "Terror da Vermelha", the column "Geleia Geral" and the controversial Cinema Novo X Marginal, among other passages important aspects of Brazilian culture in the 60s and 70s.

credits.title: Candango: Memoirs from a Festival
credits.overview: In 1965, a year after the military coup in Brazil, an oasis of freedom opened in the country's capital. The Brasília Film Festival: a landmark of cultural and political resistance. Its story is that of Brazilian cinema itself.

credits.title: Arroz, Feijão e Cinema
credits.overview: Arroz, Feijão e Cinema is a record of the transformative impacts that a popular movie theater, Ponto Cine, brought to the lives of the population of Guadalupe and adjacent neighborhoods in the Rio suburbs through a program exclusively of Brazilian films and projects from audience formation.

credits.title: Ferreira Gullar: Arqueologia do Poeta
credits.overview: The intense life of Ferreira Gullar, one of the most influential poets in Brazil, is revisited by his personal friend Silvio Tendler, based on his most acclaimed work: Poema Sujo. credits.title: Neville D'Almeida: Chronicler of Beauty and Chaos
credits.overview: This film seeks to rescue the role of filmmaker Neville D'Almeida by using many rare images, numerous interviews, vast archival and audiovisual material.

credits.title: Memórias do Grupo Opinião
credits.overview: Follows the story of Opinião, a theatre group created in 1964 during the early Brazilian dictatorship period to oppose the government through artistic performances. credits.title: The Great Mystical Circus
credits.overview: The story of five generations of the Austrian-Brazilian Knieps family, from the inauguration of their family-owned Great Mystical Circus in the 1910s up to the early 21st century, following both the family and the circus from their prime through to their decadence.

credits.title: Brazilian Cinema in the 20th Century
credits.overview: Two years of research and visits to collections, cinematheques and museums; almost seventy interviews that generated 30 hours of recorded material; more than two hundred scanned photos and more than one hundred films watched. credits.title: Pitanga
credits.overview: This documentary investigates the aesthetic, political and existential trajectory of emblematic Black Brazilian actor Antônio Pitanga. credits.title: Cinema Novo
credits.overview: A deep investigation, in the way of a poetic essay, on one of the main Latin American movements in cinema, analyzed via the thoughts of its main authors, who invented, in the early 1960s, a new way of making movies in Brazil, with a political attitude, always near to people's problems, that combined art and revolution.

credits.title: Cordilheiras no Mar: A Fúria do Fogo Bárbaro
Tudo Por Amor ao Cinema
credits.overview: A documentary on Cosme Alves Netto (1937-1996), former head of the Cinematheque of the Museum of Modern Arts at Rio de Janeiro.

credits.title: River of Faith - An Encounter with Pope Francis
credits.overview: The documentary talks about World Youth Day, held in Rio de Janeiro in 2013. The event was Pope Francis' first trip abroad and brought together more than 3 million young people from around the world. credits.title: Dossiê Jango
credits.overview: João Goulart (known as Jango) had been democratically elected president of Brazil, but was expelled from office after the coup of April 1, 1964. credits.title: Giovanni Improtta
credits.overview: Giovanni Improtta is a criminal who wants to climb the social ladder and become a law-abiding citizen. To achieve it, he commits some more crimes He is betrayed, and ends up under the spotlight of the media and the radar of the police, falsely charged for murder.

credits.title: VINTE - RioFilme, 20 anos de cinema brasileiro
credits.overview: The documentary VINTE - RioFilme, 20 anos de cinema brasileiro is a celebration of these two decades of Brazilian cinema, revealing the role of RioFilme in its recent history. Consideração do Poema
credits.overview: Carlos Drummond de Andrade's poetry is read by exponents of Brazilian culture, such as Chico Buarque, Caetano Veloso, Adriana Calcanhoto, Fernanda Torres, Marilia Pera, Antonio Cicero and others.

credits.title: 5x Favela, Now by Ourselves

credits.title: Em Quadro: A História de 4 Negros nas Telas
credits.overview: A documentary that tells the history of 4 famous actors in Brazil.

credits.title: The Greatest Love of All
credits.overview: Antônio is an astrophysicist who has just found out he has an inoperable brain tumor. After decades living in the United States, he returns to Brazil and tries to learn more about his biological mother. His quest sends him off into the slums of Rio de Janeiro.

credits.title: Nenhum Motivo Explica a Guerra
credits.overview: Afroreggae Cultural Group DVD containing a concert and a documentary about the group's social and cultural work at the favelas in Rio de Janeiro.

credits.title: Depois do Transe
credits.overview: The documentary "Depois do Transe" covers the entire process of creating the masterpiece "Entranced Earth", which was released and awarded at the Cannes Film Festival in 1967. credits.title: Referências
credits.overview: During a showing of rare Afro-Brazilian Cinema films at the Cinematheque of the Museum of Modern Art of Rio de Janeiro, actor/filmmaker Zózimo Bulbul gathered some of the most notorious Brazilian black directors to talk about their works, their lives and their perspectives on the future.

credits.title: Looking for Black Orpheus
credits.overview: Documentary about Marcel Camus' 1959 film Black Orpheus, its cultural and musical roots, and its resonance in Brazil today.

credits.title: Coisa Mais Linda - Histórias e Casos da Bossa Nova
credits.overview: Documentary about the birth of bossa-nova, in Brazil, and the major stars of this musical style.

credits.title: Glauber Rocha - The Movie, Brazil's Labyrinth
credits.overview: Documentary about Brazilian filmmaker Glauber Rocha, one of the most important names in the Cinema Novo, with interviews with some of his friends and colleagues.

credits.title: God Is Brazilian
credits.overview: God decides to take a vacation, but first He has to find a saint who can rule the universe while He's away. So He goes to the Northeast of Brazil, where He believes there's a very good man for the job. As soon as He comes down to Earth, a young man comes along to help on His quest.

credits.title: At the Edge of the Earth
credits.overview: On 17 May 1931, the young director Mário Peixoto released his masterpiece "Limite" in a premiere in Capitólio Theater in Rio de Janeiro to astonished audiences bewildered by the impressive and poetic images. Considered by many viewers the best Brazilian movie ever made, this feature has never been released commercially

credits.title: 1968 - Without Losing Tenderness
credits.overview: The story of the University of Brasília, since it was only a project in Darcy Ribeiro's head until the fateful events in August 1968 when its campus was invaded by the police, during the military dictatorship, thus putting an end to its independence.

credits.title: Orfeu
credits.overview: Orfeu is a popular composer from a samba school. He lives in the favela and falls madly in love when he meets Euridice, a newcomer to the neighborhood. But the local drug boss Lucinho stands between them and will drastically change both their lives.

credits.title: For All - O Trampolim da Vitória
credits.overview: 1943, World War II. The northeastern coast of Brazil is an strategic region for the Allies. credits.title: Dib
credits.overview: Documentary that addresses, through the testimony of directors and actors, the work of Dib Lutfi, considered one of the greatest photographers of Brazilian cinema.

credits.title: Nelson Sargento
credits.overview: Biographical portrait of samba dancer Nelson Sargento in Morro da Mangueira, Rio de Janeiro.

credits.title: Tieta of Agreste
credits.overview: After being exiled for 26 years, Tieta returns to her native village in Bahia, bringing chaos and upheaving the local order.

credits.title: Rio's Love Song
credits.overview: Four love stories which portray a wide gamut of emotions and desires against the backdrop of Rio de Janeiro. credits.title: Better Days Ahead
credits.overview: Earning her living by dubbing American TV Series, a woman dreams of becoming an international Hollywood star.

credits.title: Alex Viany - Um Documentário em Vídeo
Luzia Homem
credits.overview: After witnessing the assassination of her parents, Luzia is raised by a cowboy and starts behaving like the men of Brazilian "Sertão". As a grown-up, she sets out to find her parent's murderer, but ends up discovering love.

credits.title: Subway to the Stars
credits.overview: In this highly stylized Brazilian drama a sax player fondly remembers one wonderful night spent with his life's love and decides to find her again. He embarks upon a quest through the wild streets of Rio to find her. Along the way he meets an assortment of odd urban underworld characters.

credits.title: Quilombo
credits.overview: Quilombo dos Palmares was a real-life democratic society, created in Brazil in the 17th century. This incredibly elaborate (and surprisingly little-known) film traces the origins of Quilombo, which began as a community of freed slaves. credits.title: Claves, 1: How Tasty Was My Little Frenchman
credits.overview: Documentary in four parts on Latin American cinema. First episode: the influences of Cahiers du cinéma, the New Wave, Italian neorealism. In Brazil, Cinema Novo draws inspiration from these models while drawing on the historical and cultural singularity of the country. The documentary was awarded the Prix Makhila d’or

credits.title: Claves, 2: We will return younger
credits.overview: Documentary in four parts on Latin American cinema. Second episode, evoking the border between fiction and documentary. With his film Tire dié (1960), the Argentinian Fernando Birri proposed this manifesto: to create a realistic and critical national cinema, closer to society without falling into populism.

credits.title: Claves, 3: Small mother country, great mother country
credits.overview: Documentary in four parts on Latin American cinema. Third episode: from the 1960s, France and Europe showed a real enthusiasm for Latin American cinema, but the latter remained hampered by numerous economic and political obstacles.

credits.title: Cinématon IX
credits.overview: Reel 9 of Gérard Courant's on-going Cinematon series.

credits.title: Filmando Bye Bye Brasil
credits.overview: Behind the scenes of the filming of the feature film Bye Bye Brasil by Cacá Diegues.

credits.title: Na Boca do Mundo
credits.overview: A black fisherman now working at a local gas station, Antônio lives at the small beach town of Atafona. His biggest ambition is to stash enough money to leave to a big city with his fiancee, a mix-raced girl who sells fresh crabs to locals and wishes for a better life. credits.title: Summer Showers
credits.overview: 70-year-old widower living in a poor Rio de Janeiro suburb falls in love again when he finds a woman of approximately the same age.

credits.title: Xica
credits.overview: The romanced story of Xica da Silva, a slave that used her "feminine atributes" in order to get power.

credits.title: The Star Rises
credits.overview: A veteran popular singer remembers her early days before fame as a humble woman who faced many obstacles in order to achieve fame, notoriety and make her dreams come true. Her life, the songs, the men she knew and helped her on her ladder to success all have a big influence on her life.

credits.title: Joanna Francesa
credits.overview: Joana is a sophisticated, beautiful woman, so she has a choice of lovers, and destinies. She will let down Pierre, the French consul at São Paulo, and with him the frivolity of tea-parties and comfort. credits.title: The Suns of Easter Island
credits.overview: Six people find a mysterious mark in the center of their left hand and all independently go to Easter Island in hopes to uncover the mystery.

credits.title: When Carnaval Comes
credits.overview: Music manager has to get three of his artists together for a special show, but soon finds out it isn't an easy task.

credits.title: The Heirs
credits.overview: Jorge, an ambitious journalist, marries into money and betrays colleagues to become a powerful politician during political turmoil in 1946 Brazil.

credits.title: Capitu
credits.overview: Adaptation of Machado de Assis’s classic novel “Dom Casmurro”. Bentinho and Capitu are friends since childhood and end up marrying. But Bentinho destroys his life when he starts suspecting Capitu has an affair with his best friend and that his son is not really his.

credits.title: Adorável Trapalhão
credits.overview: Epitácio is the driver of a widower musical entrepreneur. Concerned with the boss' happiness, Epitácio tries to find him a wife and introduces him to Lucy, the children's teacher, who dreams of becoming a singer.

credits.title: Improvised and Purposeful: Cinema Novo
credits.overview: Originally produced for German TV, Improvised and Purposeful is a firsthand look at the "Cinema Novo" movement (otherwise known as the 'Brazilian New Wave'). Director Joaquim Pedro de Andrade focuses on six Cinema Novo filmmakers working in Rio in 1967.

credits.title: Oito Universitários
credits.overview: The political activity of students in the 60s.

credits.title: The Big City
credits.overview: In search of a better life, Luzia leaves the Northeast of Brazil and goes to Rio de Janeiro, looking for her fiance who went first to pave their way. Alone in the Marvelous City, she is forced to accept the friendship and protection of Calunga and, later, the company of Inácio.

credits.title: O Circo
credits.overview: The documentary follows a caravan of acrobats through the suburbs of Rio de Janeiro, presenting the situation of circuses in Brazil through testimonies from several circus artists.

credits.title: Ganga Zumba
credits.overview: The life of a runaway slave who founded the Quilombo dos Palmares, an outlaw community of Brazilian slaves.

credits.title: Five Times Favela
credits.overview: Five segments about the hardships faced by people living in slums on hills in Rio de Janeiro.
